claim: Tuberculosis kills more than 1 million humans each year.

claim: In the majority of exposed people, inhaled MTB is either killed by the innate immune system of the lung or triggers the development of granuloma structures around infected cells.
source: In the majority of exposed people, inhaled MTB is either killed by the innate immune system of the lung or triggers the development of granuloma structures around infected cells (Pai et al., 2016).

claim: It is estimated that more than a quarter of the world's population is latently infected with MTB.
source: It is estimated that more than a quarter of the world's population is latently infected with MTB.

claim: The life-long risk to develop reactivation tuberculosis is around 5% and is influenced by a variety of genetic and environmental factors.

claim: Parasitic helminth infections affect an estimated number of >2 billion humans.

claim: Protective immunity to MTB requires robust Th1 immunity and is possibly enhanced by Th17 cells.
source: Immune responses to helminths in general are characterized by a strong Th2 component with production of IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, IL-10, and IgE (Babu and Nutman, 2016), whereas protective immunity to MTB requires robust Th1 immunity and is possibly enhanced by Th17 cells (Gopal et al., 2012; Monin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established immunological knowledge and is supported by citations.

claim: Helminth infection of household contacts of patients with active, smear-positive tuberculosis increased the rate of tuberculin skin test conversion indicating a higher risk to become infected.

claim: Experimental infection of mice with Schistosoma mansoni or Heligmosomoides polygyrus impaired Th1 cell generation after vaccination with BCG.
